sections.h2: Where is Newberry County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Newberry County is in central South Carolina and covers 647.28 square miles, of which 630.29 are land. It is bordered by Union, Fairfield, Lexington, Richland, Saluda, Greenwood and Laurens counties.

The city of Newberry is the county seat and largest community. Chappells, Stoney Hill, Jalapa and Kinards, which is partly in Laurens County, are other named communities. Some of the county falls inside the Belfast Wildlife Management Area and the Sumter National Forest, so not every acre is available to build on or buy.

The 2020 census counted 37,719 residents in 15,039 households, with a median age of 43.1, and the 2025 estimate is 39,561. It is a small county, with about 30,400 parcels according to the Assessor, so most sales are local ones.

sections.h2: What is the history of Newberry County?
sections.html:
Newberry County was formed in 1785 from the Ninety-Six District, and the town of Newberry was founded in 1789 as its seat. The origin of the name is unknown, though one theory ties it to Quaker settlers and Newbury Park in London.

Cotton was the main crop before the Civil War. The railroad reached the county in the early 1850s, the Lutheran Church founded Newberry College in 1856, and the first cotton mills opened in the 1880s.

Fighting in the Revolution came before the county existed: Williams' Plantation on December 31, 1780, Mud Lick on March 2, 1781, and Bush River in May 1781. The population has risen from 29,416 in 1960 to 37,719 in 2020, a slow climb compared with the Columbia suburbs to the southeast.

Mill-era streets and farm-to-market roads mean a lot of houses here are decades old, with original wiring, plumbing and roofs. Those are the systems buyers' lenders ask about, and they are the ones owners put off fixing.

sections.h2: What do Newberry County residents do for work?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest employment sector in Newberry County, with 5,019 of 14,670 jobs in the third quarter of 2023, or 34.2 percent. Those jobs paid an average of $58,188, above the countywide average of $46,191.

  • Health care and social assistance: 1,484 jobs, 10.1 percent
  • Retail trade: 1,477 jobs, 10.1 percent
  • Educational services: 1,178 jobs, 8.0 percent

The employers named as of April 2024 were Caterpillar, Georgia-Pacific, Komatsu, Kraft Foods, Newberry College, Samsung Electronics, Valmont Industries and Walmart. The county's 2022 gross domestic product was $1.8 billion. Because so many jobs sit in a few plants, a layoff or relocation can leave a household selling quickly, often with tax and mortgage payments already behind.

sections.h2: Which Newberry County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Delinquent Tax Collector share the same address in Newberry: 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. The county administrative office is at 1309 College Street.

OfficeContact
Assessor803-321-2125, option 1; assessorsoffice@newberrycounty.gov; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
Delinquent Tax Collector(803) 321-2128; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
County administration803-321-2100; 1309 College Street

The Assessor's page says the office maintains ownership, valuation and assessment for all real property, about 30,400 parcels including mobile and manufactured homes. It offers forms for legal residence, mailing address change, agricultural use and a Notice of Objection. Ask the Treasurer for the due date printed on your bill, since we could not confirm it on an opened county page.

sections.h2: How do penalties work on a Newberry County tax bill?
sections.html:
Newberry County follows the state penalty schedule in S.C. Code 12-45-180, which adds 3 percent starting January 16, another 7 percent on February 2, and another 5 percent on March 17, when the Treasurer may also issue a tax execution.

The county pages we opened do not restate those dates, so confirm them against your own bill. What the Delinquent Tax Office does say is that it collects delinquent taxes through all legal avenues, files bankruptcy claims in federal court and files claims with the Probate Court. That last item matters for inherited houses: an estate with unpaid tax can find a claim waiting in probate.

The office also uses American Financial Credit Services to collect some personal property taxes. Once an account is placed with that firm, it cannot be paid to the county until the firm is paid, and the firm's fee is added.

sections.h2: How does the Newberry County tax sale work?
sections.html:
Newberry County holds an annual delinquent tax sale. The county page lists the 2026 sale for Monday, November 9, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., with registration at 9:00 a.m., at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus, 1922 Wilson Road.

Key details from the county page:

  • Pre-registration ran October 21 through November 6, 2026, in person at 1512 Martin Street or by email with a copy of photo ID.
  • Properties are advertised for three consecutive weeks before the sale in The Newberry Observer.
  • Mobile homes are included in the yearly tax sale.

Under S.C. Code 12-51-90 the owner can redeem within twelve months of the sale. Redemption interest runs 3 percent of the bid in the first quarter, 6 in the second, 9 in the third and 12 in the fourth. If nobody redeems, the buyer gets a deed. An owner who sees a sale coming can sell the house first, and the title company pays the county out of the proceeds.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Newberry County assessment?
sections.html:
You file a Notice of Objection with the Assessor, and state law sets the deadline at 90 days after the assessor mails the notice. Newberry County's assessor page offers the objection form but states no deadline of its own.

The state statute lets owners object to fair market value, special use value or the assessment ratio. An owner who got no notice may appeal in writing at any time; filing before the first penalty date applies to the current year, and filing later applies to the next one.

The Assessor's page also urges new owners who live in the house to file early for the legal residence classification. State law says the 4 percent ratio applies to an owner-occupied home that is not rented more than 72 days a year, and the application must be filed before the first penalty date. Miss it and the 6 percent ratio applies for that year, which can overstate the tax portion of a buyer's mortgage payment.

sections.h2: What should a Newberry County seller do first?
sections.html:
Start by finding out exactly what is owed and which office holds it. A short call to the right office saves weeks later.

  • Call the Assessor at 803-321-2125, option 1, to confirm the owner of record, mailing address and whether the legal residence form is on file.
  • Call the Delinquent Tax Collector at (803) 321-2128 if any year is past due, and ask for a payoff good through the expected closing date.
  • If the owner has died, ask whether the Delinquent Tax Office has filed a claim with the Probate Court.
  • Check whether a tax sale notice has been advertised in The Newberry Observer.

Newberry County's Assessor also notes that agricultural use applies to qualifying tracts used to commercially grow crops or timber. If part of the land you are selling carries that special valuation, ask the office what a change of use or sale does to the value before you sign a contract.

faqs.q: Where is the Newberry County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: It is at 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. The phone is 803-321-2125, option 1, and the office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent taxes in Newberry County?
faqs.a: The Delinquent Tax Collector, at 1512 Martin Street. The phone number is (803) 321-2128.

faqs.q: When is the Newberry County tax sale?
faqs.a: The county's page lists Monday, November 9, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus. Dates change each year, so check with the office.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Newberry County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written Notice of Objection with the Assessor. State law allows 90 days from the mailing of the assessment notice.

faqs.q: Can I redeem my house after a Newberry County tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, within twelve months of the sale, by paying the taxes, costs and interest set by S.C. Code 12-51-90.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newberry County house that owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing. Ask the Delinquent Tax Office for a payoff before the closing date.
